neighbor_rows.label: Serine hydrolase nucleophile elbow
neighbor_rows.summary: Catalytic nucleophile serine of serine hydrolases, specifically the conserved “nucleophile elbow” pentapeptide (e.g., GXSXG/GHSxG/GDSL) at a β→α junction in α/β‑hydrolase–like folds, across esterases/lipases/thioesterases and related serine proteases/transferases; the feature recognizes this structural/sequence motif even in inactive esterase‑like homologs.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Catalytic nucleophile serine of serine hydrolases, specifically the conserved “nucleophile elbow” pentapeptide (e.g., GXSXG/GHSxG/GDSL) at a β→α junction in α/β‑hydrolase–like folds, across esterases/lipases/thioesterases and related serine proteases/transferases; the feature recognizes this structural/sequence motif even in inactive esterase‑like homologs.
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks centered on a single serine in a short coil at the end of a β‑strand entering an α‑helix (β→α turn); occasional weak shoulders on immediately adjacent small residues or nearby loop positions; other catalytic‑triad residues (Asp/His) are typically not activated. Most proteins show 1–4 peaks, with multi‑modular assembly‑line enzymes showing one per TE/catalytic module.
Exemplars: - Siderophore esterases/trilactone hydrolases (IroE/IroD family): peak on the nucleophilic Ser at the β→α junction.
- BioH-like pimeloyl‑ACP methyl ester esterases: sharp peak on the annotated catalytic Ser; Asp/His of the triad remain silent.
- Mammalian BPHL/carboxylesterase-like hydrolases: dominant peak on the catalytic Ser with minor signal on an adjacent substrate‑binding residue.
- NRPS/PKS thioesterase domains: activation on the Ser within the GHSxG motif; multiple peaks in multi‑module systems.
- Cholinesterases and carboxylesterases: activation on the catalytic Ser in the GXSXG nucleophile elbow.
- Serine carboxypeptidases and dipeptidyl peptidases (α/β‑hydrolase catalytic domains): peak on the active‑site Ser.
- Mycobacterial Ag85 mycolyltransferases (SGNH/GDSL hydrolase‑like): activation on the catalytic Ser of the SGNH/GDSL motif.
- Inactive esterase‑like/pseudoenzymes: residual activation on the conserved nucleophile‑elbow serine despite loss of catalytic activity.

neighbor_rows.label: Secretory phosphoserine hotspots
neighbor_rows.summary: The feature marks specific phosphoserine sites in the N-terminal mature region of secreted enamel matrix and related secreted proteins, consistent with FAM20C-type secretory phosphorylation hotspots; signals can also occur within structured domains (e.g., beta strands of RRMs).
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: The feature marks specific phosphoserine sites in the N-terminal mature region of secreted enamel matrix and related secreted proteins, consistent with FAM20C-type secretory phosphorylation hotspots; signals can also occur within structured domains (e.g., beta strands of RRMs).
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks on Ser, often at known or predicted secretory-pathway phosphoserine sites located shortly after the signal peptide cleavage site of secreted proteins. Within globular domains, activations can localize to beta strands and be sparse on helices or disordered tails. The number of peaks per protein is typically small (one to a few), with the strongest peak flanked by lower-activation residues in the immediate sequence neighborhood.
Exemplars: Enamel matrix proteins (amelogenin, enamelin, ameloblastin, odontogenic ameloblast-associated protein): N-terminal phosphoserine sites just downstream of the signal peptide; Follicular dendritic cell secreted peptide: clustered Ser activations in the mature N-terminal region; Poly(A)-binding proteins (RRM RNA-binding proteins): discrete Ser sites on beta strands within RRM1/RRM2; Ser/Thr kinases, phosphatases, and phospho-regulatory proteins: regulatory Ser/Thr sites; DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferases (DNMT/Dcm): Ser/Thr sites implicated in regulation; Plant bZIP/bHLH transcription factors: Ser/Thr phospho-motifs in activation/regulatory regions; Vesicle-trafficking and cytoskeletal adaptors/scaffolds (e.g., CKAP2L): discrete Ser sites in low-complexity linkers; Undecaprenyl-diphosphatases (bacterial): Ser/Thr motifs in extracytoplasmic loops or N-terminal regions; Membrane proteins and ion channels: cytosolic Ser/Thr segments; Purine nucleoside phosphorylase family and translation-related components: scattered Ser/Thr sites within structured regions.

neighbor_rows.label: ABC NBD LSGGQ C-loop
neighbor_rows.summary: ABC transporter NBD signature (C‑loop) motif recognition—specifically the conserved LSGGQ segment, with strongest focus on the serine preceding the Gly‑Gly pair—plus weaker sensitivity to adjacent ATP‑site elements (notably the Walker A/P‑loop)
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: ABC transporter NBD signature (C‑loop) motif recognition—specifically the conserved LSGGQ segment, with strongest focus on the serine preceding the Gly‑Gly pair—plus weaker sensitivity to adjacent ATP‑site elements (notably the Walker A/P‑loop)
Activation pattern: Residue‑level peaks centered on the Ser of the LSGGQ signature at a loop→helix junction within ABC/ABC‑like ATPase nucleotide‑binding domains; occasional low signals on the flanking Gly/Gln and nearby ATP‑site residues (Walker A/P‑loop; sometimes an adjacent Asp from the D‑loop). Proteins with two NBDs show two such peaks; minimal to no activation outside NBDs or in transmembrane regions.
Exemplars: - Spermidine/putrescine importer PotA (ABC importer NBD): strong on the LSGGQ Ser; minor at the Walker A region.
- Cobalt importer CbiO (ABC importer NBD): strong on the LSGGQ Ser; weak signals in the P‑loop and a nearby β‑strand.
- Peptide exporter SkfE (ABC exporter NBD): peak at the LSGGQ‑region Ser; weak within the annotated ATP‑binding loop.
- Antigen peptide transporter TAP1 (eukaryotic ABC exporter NBD): strong at the LSGGQ Ser; additional weak activation in the Walker A GxxxxGKS/T segment.
- ABC transporter I family member (bacterial ABC NBD): dominant peak at the LSGGQ Ser; minor at ATP‑binding stretch.
- ABCE1/RLI1 (ABC‑like ATPase with two NBDs, ribosome recycling): two strong peaks at the Ser of each LSGG… signature; weaker signals at each domain’s Walker A region.

neighbor_rows.label: ABC NBD beta1 strand
neighbor_rows.summary: Conserved N-terminal β-strand of ABC nucleotide-binding domains (β1), immediately upstream of the Walker A P-loop and adjacent to the A-loop aromatic residue, shared by ABC ATPases across transport and non-transport families.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Conserved N-terminal β-strand of ABC nucleotide-binding domains (β1), immediately upstream of the Walker A P-loop and adjacent to the A-loop aromatic residue, shared by ABC ATPases across transport and non-transport families.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks on single polar/acidic residues (most often S/N/D, with frequent H/G neighbors) within this β-strand of the ABC domain; typically one sharp peak per NBD. In bacterial single-NBD proteins the peak lies near the extreme N-terminus (~positions 5–30); in long eukaryotic ABC transporters two widely separated peaks appear (one per NBD). Peaks sit in β-sheet elements with high structural confidence and do not coincide with the Walker A lysine or other annotated ATP-binding residues.
Exemplars: - Energy-coupling factor (ECF) transporter A subunits (EcfA1/EcfA2): strong S peak in the NBD β-strand with neighboring D/H also activated.
- Peptide/bacteriocin secretion ABC exporters (e.g., SkfE): S at the N-terminal β-strand of the ABC domain; no activation on the Walker A site.
- Multidrug ABC transporters with tandem NBDs (e.g., YbhF-like): identical peaks near the start of each ABC domain (D/N in β-strand), one per NBD.
- ABCB7 iron–sulfur cluster exporter: S within an LSGIS segment located between the A-loop Tyr and the Walker A motif, consistent with the β-strand preceding the P-loop.
- ABCD4 cobalamin transporter: S in a β-sheet of the C-terminal NBD, distinct from the annotated ATP-binding site.
- ABCI/ABCI11 family (ECF-like/plant plastid ABCI subunits): N in the NBD β-strand just upstream of the Walker A region; targeting peptides show no activation.

neighbor_rows.label: HRD-DKP kinase catalytic loop
neighbor_rows.summary: Canonical protein kinase catalytic loop motif (subdomain VIb–VII), centered on the HRD motif and the immediately following DKP residues (consensus HRD[L/V]KP), often extending toward the downstream DFG glycine; marks the active-site proton-acceptor Asp and adjacent Lys/Pro that shape the kinase active site across Ser/Thr, Tyr, dual-specificity, and kinase-like/pseudokinases in diverse taxa.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Canonical protein kinase catalytic loop motif (subdomain VIb–VII), centered on the HRD motif and the immediately following DKP residues (consensus HRD[L/V]KP), often extending toward the downstream DFG glycine; marks the active-site proton-acceptor Asp and adjacent Lys/Pro that shape the kinase active site across Ser/Thr, Tyr, dual-specificity, and kinase-like/pseudokinases in diverse taxa.
Activation pattern: Short, contiguous windows (~8–15 aa) within kinase domains with residue-level peaks at the Lys located two residues C‑terminal to the catalytic Asp (HRD→K), with secondary activation on the His/Asp of HRD and the following Pro; frequently includes a nearby downstream Gly (from the DFG motif). Typically one peak per kinase domain, with occasional multiple clusters in multi-kinase or repeated architectures.
Exemplars: - MAPK pathway kinase (MEK5/MAP2K): activation on the catalytic loop; peak at Lys two residues after the catalytic Asp.
- Cell‑cycle inhibitory kinase (WEE/Myt1 family): catalytic loop highlighted; Lys peak two residues C‑terminal to the active‑site Asp, spanning loop-to-helix transition.
- eIF2α kinase (PKR): localized to catalytic loop near the active‑site Asp; sharp peak at adjacent Lys and surrounding DKP residues.
- Plant serine/threonine kinase: activation across the D–K–P segment of the catalytic loop with a Lys peak; extends into the following helix and often toward DFG Gly.
- Vps15 serine/threonine protein kinase: N‑terminal kinase domain catalytic loop; peak at Lys two residues after the proton‑acceptor Asp.

neighbor_rows.label: SAM-binding glycine-rich loop
neighbor_rows.summary: Conserved S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) cofactor-binding glycine-rich loop (motif I) of Rossmann-like SAM-dependent methyltransferase domains, typically the N‑terminal GxG loop flanked by hydrophobic and acidic residues that form the SAM-binding site
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Conserved S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) cofactor-binding glycine-rich loop (motif I) of Rossmann-like SAM-dependent methyltransferase domains, typically the N‑terminal GxG loop flanked by hydrophobic and acidic residues that form the SAM-binding site
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks on one or a few glycines within the motif I loop (often a GxG pair), with occasional signal on an adjacent acidic residue (D/E) and spillover onto the preceding beta-strand; usually near the N-terminus of the MTase domain, or internal in multidomain proteins
Exemplars: - tRNA 5-carboxymethoxyuridine methyltransferase (Trm family): peak on the SAM-binding glycine in motif I, with minor activation on the preceding beta-strand
- Ubiquinone/Coenzyme Q O-methyltransferase (UbiE/Coq family): peak on the SAM-binding glycine and nearby D/E within the binding site loop
- Small RNA 2'-O-methyltransferase (Hen1-like): peak on the SAM-binding glycine in motif I, plus weaker signal on a nearby SAM-binding D/E
- mRNA cap N7 methyltransferases (eukaryotic and viral): activation on the conserved N-terminal GxG loop of the SAM-binding site
- Type II DNA N6-adenine/N4-cytosine methyltransferases: activation on the N-terminal glycine-rich SAM-binding loop
- Osmoprotectant small-molecule methyltransferases (glycine/sarcosine/dimethylglycine): activation on the motif I SAM-binding glycine(s)
- Protein arginine methyltransferases: activation on the Rossmann-like SAM-binding GxG loop

neighbor_rows.label: Phosphate-coupling Ser/Thr residues
neighbor_rows.summary: Conserved phosphate-coupling serine/threonine residues in phosphotransfer and NTP-handling enzymes—most prominently the receiver-domain “switch” Thr/Ser of two‑component response regulators, the Walker‑A Thr/Ser of P‑loop NTPases, and the Thr in the HAD DxDT/V catalytic motif—with analogous Ser/Thr positions flagged in histidine kinase catalytic regions and other ATP/phosphate‑processing domains.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Conserved phosphate-coupling serine/threonine residues in phosphotransfer and NTP-handling enzymes—most prominently the receiver-domain “switch” Thr/Ser of two‑component response regulators, the Walker‑A Thr/Ser of P‑loop NTPases, and the Thr in the HAD DxDT/V catalytic motif—with analogous Ser/Thr positions flagged in histidine kinase catalytic regions and other ATP/phosphate‑processing domains.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks focused on individual Ser/Thr, often with smaller signals on nearby Asp/Gly; in response regulators the main peak is a Thr/Ser around positions 80–90 within a β‑strand; in histidine kinases, peaks cluster in the cytosolic kinase (CA/DHp) region at higher sequence positions; in P‑loop enzymes, at the Walker‑A P‑loop; in HAD phosphatases, at motif I (DxDT/V). Multiple residues per protein can be flagged; disordered regions are generally avoided; occasional Asp peaks occur, especially in response regulators.
Exemplars: - Two-component response regulators (CheY-like): marks the conserved “switch” Thr/Ser (CheY T87 equivalent) in the β4–β5 region rather than the phosphorylated Asp.
- Histidine kinases (bacterial and eukaryotic hybrid HKs): marks Ser/Thr in the cytosolic CA/DHp kinase module near ATP-binding elements.
- HAD-like hydrolases/sugar-phosphate phosphatases: marks the Thr of the DxDT/V motif I, sometimes adjacent catalytic Asp residues.
- P-loop NTPase helicases (RecQ, SWI/SNF-like, viral helicases): marks the Walker A Thr/Ser within the GxxxxGKT/S P-loop (Thr adjacent to glycines).
- Plant pseudo-response regulators (APRR/PRR): marks the conserved receiver-domain switch Thr/Ser despite loss of the phosphorylatable Asp.
- P-type ATPases: occasional Ser/Thr hotspots in cytosolic loops at secondary-structure junctions near phosphate-handling domains.

neighbor_rows.label: HATPase_c ATP-lid turn
neighbor_rows.summary: A short β-strand-to-loop motif within the catalytic HATPase_c (CA) domain of GHKL-fold histidine kinases (and closely related GHKL ATPases), corresponding to the strand–turn at the edge of the ATP-binding site/ATP-lid. The motif is typically centered on a Ser/Thr, often preceded by acidic residues and followed by a Pro (occasionally including a His), and recurs in the C‑terminal cytosolic portion of diverse HKs.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: A short β-strand-to-loop motif within the catalytic HATPase_c (CA) domain of GHKL-fold histidine kinases (and closely related GHKL ATPases), corresponding to the strand–turn at the edge of the ATP-binding site/ATP-lid. The motif is typically centered on a Ser/Thr, often preceded by acidic residues and followed by a Pro (occasionally including a His), and recurs in the C‑terminal cytosolic portion of diverse HKs.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks on contiguous 4–8 aa windows. Activations localize to the C-terminal cytosolic HATPase_c domain, mapping to the end of a beta-strand that transitions into a coil/turn; sequences are enriched for Ser/Thr and acidic residues with a characteristic S/T–x–P pattern and sometimes an adjacent His. Multiple short windows may occur per protein. Homologous GHKL ATPases co-activate at lower scores; occasional weak hits appear in other kinases.
Exemplars: - Two-component sensor histidine kinases (e.g., alginate biosynthesis sensor KinB): activation on a short β-strand→turn in the CA (HATPase_c) domain, peak on Ser within a V–x–S–x–P pattern.
- Short-chain fatty acid/acetate-sensing histidine kinase AtoS: same β-strand→loop element in the CA domain, adjacent to residues known to affect ATP binding.
- Redox/oxygen-responsive SrrB family histidine kinases: activation on the β-strand terminus and following turn in HATPase_c, centered on Ser.
- Sporulation histidine kinase KinA (phosphorelay initiator): activation on a DSHP-containing β-strand→turn with a trailing Pro in the CA domain.
- Virulence/type III secretion regulator SsrA histidine kinase: activation on the same CA-domain β-strand→turn (Ser-centered, Pro-terminated).
- Branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase kinase (GHKL-like regulatory kinase): co-activation on the equivalent β-strand→turn bordering the ATP-binding site in its histidine-kinase-like HATPase fold.
- Chemotaxis histidine kinase CheA (soluble HK): activation on the corresponding β-strand→turn in the P4 catalytic (HATPase_c) domain.

neighbor_rows.label: SDR catalytic β–α turn
neighbor_rows.summary: Active-site β–α turn of Rossmann-fold NAD(P)-dependent dehydrogenases/reductases (especially SDRs), i.e., the short loop at the C-terminus of a β-strand that precedes the helix carrying the YXXXK motif and houses/abuts the catalytic Ser/Thr proton donor and NAD(P)/substrate contacts
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Active-site β–α turn of Rossmann-fold NAD(P)-dependent dehydrogenases/reductases (especially SDRs), i.e., the short loop at the C-terminus of a β-strand that precedes the helix carrying the YXXXK motif and houses/abuts the catalytic Ser/Thr proton donor and NAD(P)/substrate contacts
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks: a single dominant activation on a small residue (Ser/Thr/Gly/Ala/Asn/Val/Ile) in the 120–200 region within the β–α turn of the Rossmann core, often immediately adjacent to annotated catalytic or substrate/NAD(P) binding residues; occasional weaker secondary peaks on the flanking β-strand or additional NAD-binding contact sites
Exemplars: - Sphingolipid 3-ketodihydrosphingosine reductase (KDSR/TSC10; SDR): peak on the catalytic Ser (proton donor) in the β–α turn.
- Short-chain dehydrogenase AusX (SDR): peak on an Ala at the end of a β-strand entering the active-site helix; minor nearby peaks.
- SDR family member 7 (steroid/retinoid-type SDR): peak on an Asn in the β–α turn immediately adjacent to a substrate-binding Ser.
- 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase type-2 (mitochondrial SDR): peak on an Ala directly adjacent to an annotated substrate-binding Ser in the catalytic loop.
- Dihydromonapterin reductase (FolM-type SDR): peak on a Thr in the β–α connector preceding the active-site helix.
- dTDP-6-deoxy-L-talose 4-dehydrogenase (sugar-nucleotide SDR): peaks at Gly/Ala that coincide with or abut NAD+ and substrate-binding residues in the Rossmann pocket.
- Light-dependent protochlorophyllide reductase (LPOR; plant/bacterial SDR): peak on a Gly in the β–α loop near the active-site region.

neighbor_rows.label: P-loop Walker A S/T
neighbor_rows.summary: Walker A/P-loop (GxxxxGKS/T) ATP phosphate-binding motif of P-loop NTPases, most prominently the nucleotide-binding domains of ABC transporters, with strongest sensitivity to the serine/threonine immediately following the invariant lysine at the start of the P-loop helix
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Walker A/P-loop (GxxxxGKS/T) ATP phosphate-binding motif of P-loop NTPases, most prominently the nucleotide-binding domains of ABC transporters, with strongest sensitivity to the serine/threonine immediately following the invariant lysine at the start of the P-loop helix
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks in a compact 2–5 residue cluster centered on the S/T that follows the Walker A lysine, with weaker signal on the lysine itself and nearby Gly/Asn; essentially no signal on Walker B acidic residues. Typically one cluster per nucleotide-binding domain: a single cluster in bacterial/half-transporters and isolated NBDs, two clusters in full-length eukaryotic ABC proteins or ABC-type ATPases. Positions align with NBD Walker A regions (≈30–60 in bacterial NBDs; ≈450–700 and ≈1100–1350 for the two sites in large eukaryotic ABCs).
Exemplars: - ECF transporter ATP-binding protein (EcfA2): activation on the Walker A patch, peaking at S adjacent to the conserved K within the annotated ATP-binding site.
- ABC peptide exporter (YydI): sharp peak at S at the start of the Walker A helix overlapping the ATP-binding annotation.
- Tyrosine transport ABC ATP-binding protein: peak at S within the GxxxxGKS/T segment at the coil-to-helix transition of the P-loop.
- Nickel transport ABC ATP-binding protein (NikD): peak at S in the annotated Walker A motif with minor signal on the adjacent K.
- Yeast elongation factor 3 (ABC-type ATPase): two discrete peaks at the S directly after the conserved K in each of the two ABC NBD Walker A motifs.
- CydD ABC transporter NBD: localized peak at S near the conserved K within the annotated ATP-binding (Walker A) region.

neighbor_rows.label: Adenosyl cofactor acidic anchors
neighbor_rows.summary: Conserved acidic residues (Asp/Glu), often paired with a nearby Ser/Thr, that anchor and/or catalyze at nucleotide‑cofactor binding sites in dinucleotide‑utilizing enzymes—most prominently the adenosyl‑moiety binding acids of NAD(P)‑dependent oxidoreductases (e.g., SDR family) and SAM‑dependent methyltransferases (Class I and related), including enzymes that tailor carbohydrates and secondary metabolites
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Conserved acidic residues (Asp/Glu), often paired with a nearby Ser/Thr, that anchor and/or catalyze at nucleotide‑cofactor binding sites in dinucleotide‑utilizing enzymes—most prominently the adenosyl‑moiety binding acids of NAD(P)‑dependent oxidoreductases (e.g., SDR family) and SAM‑dependent methyltransferases (Class I and related), including enzymes that tailor carbohydrates and secondary metabolites
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue‑level peaks (typically 2–4 per protein) centered on acidic side chains in the N‑terminal/mid regions (~50–150), with occasional secondary peaks later in the domain (~230–300). Peaks often occur as Asp/Glu with a neighboring Ser/Thr, mapping to glycine‑rich/loop regions of nucleotide‑cofactor pockets; multidomain enzymes can show multiple such sites.
Exemplars: - Short‑chain dehydrogenase/reductase (SDR) oxidoreductases (e.g., 3‑oxoacyl‑ACP reductases, sugar epimerases): activation on the β‑loop acidic residue adjacent to the Rossmann glycine‑rich loop that binds the adenosyl ribose of NAD(H)/NADP(H), often with a nearby Ser/Thr.
- Class I SAM‑dependent RNA methyltransferases (rRNA/tRNA/snRNA MTases such as KsgA/Dim1 and many Trm/Trm‑like enzymes): activation on the conserved acidic residues in the SAM‑binding/catalytic motifs (e.g., motif I Asp and/or motif IV Asp) near the active site, sometimes with adjacent Ser/Thr.
- DNA methyltransferases (adenine and cytosine MTases): activation on the catalytic Asp of the DPPY/DPC‑like motif and neighboring Ser/Thr in the SAM‑binding loop.
- Protein methyltransferases (lysine and N‑terminal MTases, including SET/NTMT types): activation on acidic residues lining the SAM‑binding cavity that position the cofactor and acceptor.
- Plant small‑molecule O‑methyltransferases in tocopherol/chlorophyll/sulfolipid pathways: activation on the SAM‑binding acidic residue near the N‑terminal nucleotide‑binding loop.
- Actinobacterial tailoring enzymes in secondary metabolism (O‑methyltransferases and NAD‑dependent ketoreductases/epimerases): activation on the acidic cofactor‑binding residues of their SAM or NAD(P) sites.

neighbor_rows.label: Acidic active-site catalytic centers
neighbor_rows.summary: Acidic active-site catalytic centers that drive phospho-/nucleotidyl reactions and related ester hydrolyses; the feature highlights Asp/Glu that coordinate catalytic metal ions and/or act as the general base, with adjacent partners (His in HxD/HRD motifs, Lys for nucleotide anchoring, Asn for stabilization). Metal coordination (Mg2+/Mn2+) is common in kinases, phosphatases, nucleases, and nucleotidyl cyclases, but the same acidic pattern can also mark metal-independent Asp-based hydrolases (e.g., hotdog/ACP thioesterases).
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Acidic active-site catalytic centers that drive phospho-/nucleotidyl reactions and related ester hydrolyses; the feature highlights Asp/Glu that coordinate catalytic metal ions and/or act as the general base, with adjacent partners (His in HxD/HRD motifs, Lys for nucleotide anchoring, Asn for stabilization). Metal coordination (Mg2+/Mn2+) is common in kinases, phosphatases, nucleases, and nucleotidyl cyclases, but the same acidic pattern can also mark metal-independent Asp-based hydrolases (e.g., hotdog/ACP thioesterases).
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks on a small set of D/E (with nearby H/K/N) within the catalytic domain; sparse focused clusters marking catalytic and, when applicable, metal-binding positions.
Exemplars: - Ser/Thr and dual-specificity kinases: highlights HRD Asp, DFG Asp, and β3 Lys. - Inositol-1-monophosphatase: highlights metal-chelating D/E. - DEDDh proofreading exonucleases: highlights acidic two-metal center. - Thioesterases (hotdog/ACP): highlights catalytic Asp (and nearby Asn) that activate water for thioester hydrolysis without metals.

neighbor_rows.label: DFG-like activation-loop triad
neighbor_rows.summary: Activation of the activation-loop gatekeeper triad in protein kinase-fold domains—recognizing canonical DFG and close variants (DLG/DYG/DWG) as well as pseudokinase swaps occupying the same position (e.g., GFE in MLKL)—across Ser/Thr, Tyr, dual-specificity, bacterial eSTKs, viral kinases, and kinase-like/pseudokinases.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Activation of the activation-loop gatekeeper triad in protein kinase-fold domains—recognizing canonical DFG and close variants (DLG/DYG/DWG) as well as pseudokinase swaps occupying the same position (e.g., GFE in MLKL)—across Ser/Thr, Tyr, dual-specificity, bacterial eSTKs, viral kinases, and kinase-like/pseudokinases.
Activation pattern: Short, highly localized windows with residue-level peaks over the triad (often G/F-enriched; acidic position can be D or E), with spillover to the following Ser/Thr/polar residue; located in the flexible activation segment; multiple peaks possible in multi-kinase-like proteins.
Exemplars: Include pseudokinases (e.g., MLKL) where the feature targets a GFE-type activation-loop triad analogous to DFG.

neighbor_rows.label: Conserved HTH aromatic residue
neighbor_rows.summary: Conserved residue within the DNA-binding helix–turn–helix (HTH) motif of bacterial transcription regulators, typically an aromatic/bulky hydrophobic residue (His, Tyr, or Phe) embedded in the recognition-helix scaffold of the HTH DNA-binding domain.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Conserved residue within the DNA-binding helix–turn–helix (HTH) motif of bacterial transcription regulators, typically an aromatic/bulky hydrophobic residue (His, Tyr, or Phe) embedded in the recognition-helix scaffold of the HTH DNA-binding domain.
Activation pattern: Predominantly single, sharp residue-level peaks within the HTH motif of the DNA-binding domain. The peak appears in the N-terminal region for regulators with N-terminal HTH domains (e.g., LysR, MarR/TetR, ArsR/SmtB, Lrp/AsnC, LacI) and in mid/C-terminal regions for regulators with C-terminal HTH domains (e.g., LuxR, two-component response regulators, NtrC-like proteins).
Exemplars: - LysR-type transcriptional activators: single peak within the N-terminal HTH motif (e.g., His/Tyr at the conserved hydrophobic position).
- LuxR-type quorum-sensing regulators (e.g., EsaR, RamA): peak within the C-terminal HTH.
- MarR/SlyA family repressors (e.g., SlyA, TcaR): peak within the winged HTH DNA-binding domain.
- ArsR/SmtB metal-response repressors: peak within the N-terminal HTH DNA-binding domain.
- Lrp/AsnC family regulators: peak in the N-terminal HTH motif.
- Two-component response regulators (e.g., SsrB): peak in the C-terminal HTH.
- NtrC-like σ54-dependent enhancer-binding proteins (e.g., ZraR): peak in the C-terminal HTH.
- LacI/CCR regulators (e.g., CcpA): peak in the N-terminal HTH motif.

neighbor_rows.label: Helix N-cap turns
neighbor_rows.summary: Short coil/turn motifs that cap or connect alpha-helices (helix-boundary “capping” sites), especially N-cap positions enriched for polar/charged residues (Ser/Thr/Asn/Gln with nearby Lys/Arg/Asp/Glu and occasional Gly/Pro), occurring in cytosolic loops of membrane proteins and in sensory/regulatory alpha-helical domains (e.g., PAS/LOV, HTH/homeobox)
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Short coil/turn motifs that cap or connect alpha-helices (helix-boundary “capping” sites), especially N-cap positions enriched for polar/charged residues (Ser/Thr/Asn/Gln with nearby Lys/Arg/Asp/Glu and occasional Gly/Pro), occurring in cytosolic loops of membrane proteins and in sensory/regulatory alpha-helical domains (e.g., PAS/LOV, HTH/homeobox)
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks on single positions or very short adjacent clusters located in coils/turns at helix boundaries (often the N-cap of the following helix). Peaks recur wherever such helix-capping turns appear; positions map to mid-sequence cytosolic loops in bacterial permeases and to PAS/HTH domains later in large eukaryotic proteins.
Exemplars: - ABC transporter permeases and drug/solute exporters: activation at cytoplasmic loop residues that N-cap or precede a transmembrane alpha-helix.
- Cell division protein FtsX: lysine in a short cytosolic loop just before a transmembrane helix (helix-boundary/cap site).
- PAS-domain sensors/regulators: 
  • Voltage-gated K+ channel (EAG) PAS: N-cap/turn residue between PAS helices. 
  • Diguanylate cyclases (c-di-GMP signaling): Ser/Thr in PAS helical linkers. 
  • cAMP-specific phosphodiesterases (e.g., PDE8A): Gln in a PAS coil between helices. 
  • Two-component histidine kinases/blue-light LOV sensors: analogous PAS/LOV helix-turn capping positions.
- Homeobox/HTH DNA-binding transcription factors: residues in the helix–turn–helix linker that cap/bridge adjacent helices within the DNA-binding domain.
- ABCA/ABCG eukaryotic transporters: cytosolic loop capping residues at the starts of transmembrane helices.

neighbor_rows.label: WD propeller E-to-coil motif
neighbor_rows.summary: Structural signature of WD-repeat beta-propellers: single, blade-internal positions at the end of a beta-strand that immediately precedes the loop/turn (E→coil junction), often adjacent to the canonical WD dipeptide and enriched for small/polar residues (G/S/T/D), across diverse eukaryotic WDR scaffolds
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Structural signature of WD-repeat beta-propellers: single, blade-internal positions at the end of a beta-strand that immediately precedes the loop/turn (E→coil junction), often adjacent to the canonical WD dipeptide and enriched for small/polar residues (G/S/T/D), across diverse eukaryotic WDR scaffolds
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks; typically one (sometimes a few) per WD blade within the high-confidence beta-sheet core; strongest on the last residue(s) of an E strand right before a loop, with occasional spillover to the first coil residue; minimal to absent in helices, disordered termini, and non-WD regions; recurrent glycine/serine/threonine/aspartate and occasional hits on the W or D of the WD motif
Exemplars: - Cilia/flagella-associated WDRs (e.g., CFAP/IFT WDRs): repeated spikes at strand termini in successive blades, sometimes at the W preceding the D of the WD motif
- U3 snoRNP/SSU processome WD proteins: discrete E→coil edge residues per blade across the WD domain
- Trm734 (WD beta-propeller regulator of tRNA methyltransferase): many blades marked by G/S/T on E-strand termini
- GID complex subunit 7 (E3 ligase adaptor): one hotspot per annotated WD repeat, mostly on beta-strand ends
- APC/C co-activators (CDC20/AMA1 family): silent disordered N-termini; activation restricted to WD-core strand-end residues across blades
- LST8 (mTOR complex subunit): distinct peaks on each WD blade at the final E residue before the loop

neighbor_rows.label: PAS sensor relay residues
neighbor_rows.summary: PAS-family sensory domains (including LOV and phytochrome PAS) — conserved polar helix‑capping/core relay positions (Asn/Ser/Thr/Asp) that transmit sensor-state changes rather than binding cofactors, recurring in N‑terminal PAS modules that regulate diverse signaling effectors (histidine kinases, ion channels, and nucleotide/c‑di‑GMP enzymes)
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: PAS-family sensory domains (including LOV and phytochrome PAS) — conserved polar helix‑capping/core relay positions (Asn/Ser/Thr/Asp) that transmit sensor-state changes rather than binding cofactors, recurring in N‑terminal PAS modules that regulate diverse signaling effectors (histidine kinases, ion channels, and nucleotide/c‑di‑GMP enzymes)
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks, typically multiple per protein, concentrated in N‑terminal PAS/LOV domains; strongest on polar residues at β–α junctions/helix N‑caps and adjacent core positions; minimal or absent in catalytic/ATP‑binding regions and at cofactor/ligand-contact residues; in large photoreceptors, additional peaks in later PAS units
Exemplars: - Two-component and hybrid histidine kinases: activation on conserved polar residues within N‑terminal PAS sensors that couple to HisKA/CA domains; often multiple PAS repeats
- LOV-domain photoreceptors (phototropins): sharp peaks on isolated serines in LOV/PAS cores near helix starts; avoids FMN-adduct and FMN‑binding residues and the downstream AGC/Ser‑Thr kinase catalytic sites
- Phytochromes: activation in PAS units of the PAS–GAF–PHY sensory module at non‑bilin‑contact relay positions
- Gas/redox PAS sensors (e.g., FixL/Dos, Aer2/HemAT): peaks in PAS cores near helical caps that transmit heme/redox state, excluding the heme‑coordinating pocket
- c-di-GMP and cyclic nucleotide signaling proteins (GGDEF/EAL/HD-GYP, cyclases/phosphodiesterases): activation in the PAS sensors fused N‑terminally to these enzymes
- Voltage-gated K+ channels of the KCNH (EAG/ERG/ELK) family: activation in the cytosolic N‑terminal PAS (eag) domain at polar relay sites
- Chemotaxis/transducer proteins: activation within cytosolic PAS sensory modules that feed into HAMP/transducer scaffolds
- Eukaryotic hybrid histidine kinases: similar PAS‑sensor polar hotspots preceding the kinase core
- Plant HD-ZIP transcription factors (not primary drivers): occasional weak activation in N‑terminal regulatory helices bearing PAS‑like helix‑capping polar motifs

neighbor_rows.label: Beta-alpha junction polar motif
neighbor_rows.summary: A coil/β-strand-to-helix junction signal: the feature activates on short polar/acidic residue clusters (enriched for Ser/Thr/Asn/Asp) at the end of β-strands and the immediately following loop, often at or near the start of a downstream α-helix. This is a generic structural motif used across many folds and families, not restricted to any one function.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: A coil/β-strand-to-helix junction signal: the feature activates on short polar/acidic residue clusters (enriched for Ser/Thr/Asn/Asp) at the end of β-strands and the immediately following loop, often at or near the start of a downstream α-helix. This is a generic structural motif used across many folds and families, not restricted to any one function.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks in short 1–3 residue clusters centered on β→loop→α transitions; the dominant maximum is typically on a Ser/Thr/Asn at the terminal strand residue or the following loop residue, with weaker secondary peaks at homologous junctions elsewhere in the same protein. Multiple such peaks recur per protein (moderate counts), rarely coincident with annotated catalytic sites.
Exemplars: - LacI-family HTH-type transcriptional regulators (TreR, FruR/Cra, PtxS, PurR, KdgR): dominant peak on a Ser/Asn near residue ~240–255 at the end of a β-strand within the C-terminal effector/regulatory (ligand-binding) domain, with weaker secondary peaks at analogous junctions around residues ~130 and ~165–170.
- D-inositol 3-phosphate glycosyltransferases (GT-B fold): strong activation on Thr in β→α linkers of the donor/acceptor-binding region, with a secondary peak near an inositol-phosphate-binding Tyr.
- Processive diacylglycerol α-glucosyltransferases: dominant peak on a Thr in the coil preceding a helix, extending into the first one or two helical residues.
- GDP-mannose-dependent mannosyltransferases (GT-A/GT-B fold): peaks on loop residues immediately before helices (multiple β→α junctions highlighted).
- ATP-dependent helicases (DNA/RNA): activation on coil segments transitioning into helices within the core helicase domains, sometimes proximal to but not overlapping Walker/P-loop or DEAH motifs.

neighbor_rows.label: Ser/Thr phosphate-binding loops
neighbor_rows.summary: Ser/Thr-centered sites in phosphate-binding loops and catalytic-domain motifs of nucleotide- and nucleic-acid–handling enzymes (Walker A/P-loop–like and analogous motifs such as the histidine‑kinase HisKA/HATPase_c regions including the ATP-lid G-boxes, PRPP/PLP loops, NAD(P)/FAD phosphate-recognition, and RNA/DNA phosphate-binding loops in nucleic-acid enzymes).
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Ser/Thr-centered sites in phosphate-binding loops and catalytic-domain motifs of nucleotide- and nucleic-acid–handling enzymes (Walker A/P-loop–like and analogous motifs such as the histidine‑kinase HisKA/HATPase_c regions including the ATP-lid G-boxes, PRPP/PLP loops, NAD(P)/FAD phosphate-recognition, and RNA/DNA phosphate-binding loops in nucleic-acid enzymes).
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks on Ser/Thr within short, flexible loops and coil–helix/strand junctions inside cytosolic catalytic domains, often near phosphate-cradling glycine-rich motifs. Little/no signal in transmembrane segments or distal structural helices such as HPt; footprint size varies from single residues to short patches. Frequently overlaps ATP/NTP-binding loops (Walker A/P-loop), the GHKL/HATPase_c ATP-lid/G-box and adjacent HisKA elements of histidine kinases, PRPP/PLP and NAD(P)/FAD phosphate-binding loops, and nucleic-acid phosphate–contacting loops.
Exemplars:
- Two-component sensor histidine kinases: activation distributed across the cytosolic Histidine kinase domain, including conserved Ser/Thr in HisKA (RTPLNG-type context) and G-boxes of the HATPase_c ATP-lid; absent in transmembranes and HPt helices.
- CRISPR-associated Cas3 helicase/nuclease and ATP-dependent RNA helicases: peaks within helicase ATP-binding domains (Walker A–adjacent loops and coil–helix junctions), not at distal nuclease motifs.
- Uracil phosphoribosyltransferase (UPRTase): focused activation on the PRPP-binding loop/helix junction.
- DNA/RNA polymerases: activation on NTP-binding loop elements that position the triphosphate.
- PLP-dependent sulfur–amino-acid enzymes: peaks on the PLP phosphate-binding loop.
- Protein tyrosine/dual-specificity phosphatases and SAM-dependent methyltransferases (NSUN/SET): activation on small phosphate-/nucleotide-adjacent catalytic loops (often centered on catalytic Cys).
- tRNA pseudouridine synthase B (TruB/Pus): activation on loops that contact the RNA phosphodiester backbone near the catalytic site.

neighbor_rows.label: Walker A P-loop motif
neighbor_rows.summary: Walker A (P-loop) phosphate-binding loop of P-loop NTPases—most prominently the ABC transporter nucleotide-binding domains—recognizing the glycine-rich GxxxxGKS/T motif in the beta1–alpha1 loop that coordinates ATP; often accompanied by a nearby downstream Q-loop glutamine in ABC NBDs
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Walker A (P-loop) phosphate-binding loop of P-loop NTPases—most prominently the ABC transporter nucleotide-binding domains—recognizing the glycine-rich GxxxxGKS/T motif in the beta1–alpha1 loop that coordinates ATP; often accompanied by a nearby downstream Q-loop glutamine in ABC NBDs
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks in a short 4–6 aa window focused on the central glycine(s) and invariant lysine of the GK-centered P-loop; localized to a flexible coil between a beta-strand and an alpha-helix; frequently appears once per NBD and thus twice in full-length eukaryotic ABC transporters; occasional weaker secondary peak at a downstream conserved glutamine (Q-loop)
Exemplars: - Energy-coupling factor (ECF) transporter ATP-binding subunit: activation on the Walker A motif (e.g., TGSGKST) within the ABC NBD; minor downstream Q-loop signal.
- Hydrophilic-compound importer (BacA-type) ABC ATPase: strong activation on the P-loop in the C-terminal NBD.
- Peptide exporter ABC ATPase (YydI-type): early N-terminal NBD P-loop peak preceding an alpha-helix.
- Vi polysaccharide exporter ABC ATPase (VexC-type): activation on the glycine-rich P-loop in the ABC domain.
- Cytochrome c biogenesis ABC ATPase (CcmA): sharp peak on the P-loop connecting beta to alpha.
- Bacterial ABC ATPase subunit (generic): primary P-loop peak with a weaker downstream Q-loop signal.
- ABCD family (peroxisomal) transporter: activation on the GPSGSGK Walker A sequence in the NBD.
- ABCC family (MRP/CFTR-like) transporter: two distinct P-loop activations, one in each NBD (e.g., GAVGSGKS and GRTGSGKS).
- ABCG family half-transporter: localized activation on the canonical Walker A loop within the NBD.

neighbor_rows.label: Glycine-rich active-site loops
neighbor_rows.summary: Conserved functional loop/turn residues at catalytic and ligand-binding sites—especially glycine-rich ATP/phosphate-binding loops and neighboring acidic (Asp/Glu) catalytic residues—more generally short coils at secondary-structure junctions that line binding pockets across regulatory and transport proteins
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Conserved functional loop/turn residues at catalytic and ligand-binding sites—especially glycine-rich ATP/phosphate-binding loops and neighboring acidic (Asp/Glu) catalytic residues—more generally short coils at secondary-structure junctions that line binding pockets across regulatory and transport proteins
Activation pattern: Sharp residue-level peaks within structured domains; enriched on glycines and Asp/Glu in coils/turns adjacent to helices/β-strands; minimal in signal peptides, disordered/low-complexity regions, and long regular helices/strands, with occasional peaks on immediately adjacent strand residues
Exemplars: - Protein kinases (bacterial/eukaryotic-like): activates on the glycine-rich ATP-binding loop (GXGXXG/Gly-loop) and the catalytic Asp region (e.g., HRD/DFG vicinity), plus nearby structured loops (as seen in SepH).
- ABC transporter NBDs: activates on Walker A P-loop (GxxxxGKS/T), Walker B acidic motif (hhhhDE), and switch/H-loop elements involved in ATP hydrolysis.
- RNA helicases (DEAD/DEAH-box): activates on the Walker/P-loop NTPase motifs and the DEAD/DEAH acidic motif within the helicase core.
- Two-component systems: in histidine kinases, on HATPase_c nucleotide-binding loops (N, G1, G2 boxes); in response regulators, on the conserved active-site Asp and adjoining loops of the receiver domain.
- HTH-type transcriptional regulators (e.g., LysR-like): activates on loop/turn residues in the central effector-binding domain (with stereotyped peaks near acidic and glycine residues) and on a loop within the N-terminal HTH region; often glycine/acidic-enriched.
- Periplasmic solute-binding proteins: activates on short coil segments flanking β/helix transitions that shape the substrate-binding cleft, with occasional peaks on adjacent strand residues.

neighbor_rows.label: Ca2+-coordinating acidic residues
neighbor_rows.summary: Ca2+-coordinating acidic residues in Ca2+-binding motifs—most strongly the canonical terminal bidentate Glu at position 12 of EF-hand loops—also including other Ca2+-ligating acidic sites (e.g., calpain/C2-like acidic clusters and channel/filter acidic motifs), plus nearby helix–loop–helix context where present.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Ca2+-coordinating acidic residues in Ca2+-binding motifs—most strongly the canonical terminal bidentate Glu at position 12 of EF-hand loops—also including other Ca2+-ligating acidic sites (e.g., calpain/C2-like acidic clusters and channel/filter acidic motifs), plus nearby helix–loop–helix context where present.
Activation pattern: Sharp, sparse residue-level peaks, typically one per Ca2+-binding site (repeating across tandem EF-hands within a protein); activations fall on acidic ligands (Glu, occasionally Asp) within EF-hand loops or other Ca2+-binding loops/short helices; weaker, sporadic peaks can appear on acidic residues in structured regions even without explicit EF-hand annotation.
Exemplars:
- Calbindin/calmodulin-like EF-hand proteins: peaks mark the Ca2+-coordinating Glu within multiple EF-hands.
- NADPH oxidase EF-hand–containing regulatory subunits: peaks on Asp/Glu within the two EF-hand motifs, including annotated Ca2+-binding sites.
- CDPK/CDPK-related kinases: strong peaks at the Ca2+-ligating Glu within each EF-hand of the C-terminal cluster; little activation in kinase/autoinhibitory regions.
- MCFD2-like two-EF-hand cofactors: precise peaks at the Ca2+-coordinating Glu in each EF-hand.
- Flagellar calcium-binding proteins with multi-EF-hand arrays: one peak per EF-hand at the C-terminal Ca2+-ligating Glu across the array, with occasional weaker signal at degenerate/ancestral sites.
- PP2A regulatory subunits (with or without explicit EF-hand annotation): peaks on acidic residues within EF-hands or EF-hand-like acidic helical contexts.
- Calpain catalytic subunits (non-EF-hand): peaks on acidic Ca2+-ligating residues within the protease core.
- Ion channels/transporters such as MCU: peaks at acidic selectivity/filter motifs (e.g., DIME motif).

neighbor_rows.label: Helix N-cap boundary residues
neighbor_rows.summary: Helix N-cap and loop-to-helix transition residues: single positions in short coil/turn segments that cap or immediately precede alpha helices (including transmembrane helices), enriched for Ser/Thr/Asp/Glu and often Pro/Gly typical of helix-capping motifs; a generic secondary-structure boundary signal rather than a family-specific functional site.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Helix N-cap and loop-to-helix transition residues: single positions in short coil/turn segments that cap or immediately precede alpha helices (including transmembrane helices), enriched for Ser/Thr/Asp/Glu and often Pro/Gly typical of helix-capping motifs; a generic secondary-structure boundary signal rather than a family-specific functional site.
Activation pattern: Punctate, residue-level peaks scattered across a protein; strongest at well-ordered coils immediately before helix starts (N-cap/N′) and at helix–helix or beta–alpha junctions, including TM-helix entry regions; generally not coincident with catalytic or ligand-binding residues.
Exemplars: - Hydratase-aldolase enzymes: loop residues directly preceding helices (repeated N-cap positions).
- P-type Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA): coils at the boundaries of transmembrane helices (before TM1, TM3, TM6, TM7, and just before TM10), plus scattered loop sites in the cytosolic headpiece.
- Menaquinone omega-hydroxylase: a loop immediately before an alpha helix (primary peak) and other secondary-structure boundary loops.
- Proteasome beta subunit: coil linkers between helices (major peaks), with a minor site in a terminal beta strand.
- Nicotinate-nucleotide adenylyltransferase: a coil just before a helix and short turns between helices; occasional weak activation in a disordered C-tail.
- 3-ketodihydrosphingosine reductase (3-KDSR): beta-to-helix turn and coils that precede helices.
- Calcineurin catalytic subunit (protein phosphatase 3): loops between beta strands and alpha helices within the catalytic domain.
- Glycerophosphodiester phosphodiesterase (GP-PDE): short, high-confidence loops connecting secondary elements (helix–helix and beta–alpha junctions) within the catalytic domain.
- Flagellar motor switch protein FliM: N-terminal coil preceding a helix in the CheY-interaction region and other helix-start loops.
- Phage SAR endolysin: turns between helices in the catalytic domain; no activation on the signal-anchor TM or catalytic residues.

neighbor_rows.label: ABC transporter NBD motifs
neighbor_rows.summary: Conserved phosphate-binding and hydrolysis motifs of nucleotide-dependent enzymes, with strongest selectivity for ABC transporter nucleotide-binding domains: Walker A P-loop (GxxxxGKT), the LSGGQ signature (C-loop), Walker B Asp/Glu pair, and the H- and Q-loops; secondarily recognizing analogous phosphotransfer/nucleotide-binding sites such as receiver-domain phospho-aspartate centers, HATPase_c ATP-binding folds of histidine kinases, and N-terminal glycine-rich Rossmann-like loops of flavin/NAD binders; also capturing catalytic motifs of c-di-GMP phosphodiesterases (EAL/HD-GYP).
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Conserved phosphate-binding and hydrolysis motifs of nucleotide-dependent enzymes, with strongest selectivity for ABC transporter nucleotide-binding domains: Walker A P-loop (GxxxxGKT), the LSGGQ signature (C-loop), Walker B Asp/Glu pair, and the H- and Q-loops; secondarily recognizing analogous phosphotransfer/nucleotide-binding sites such as receiver-domain phospho-aspartate centers, HATPase_c ATP-binding folds of histidine kinases, and N-terminal glycine-rich Rossmann-like loops of flavin/NAD binders; also capturing catalytic motifs of c-di-GMP phosphodiesterases (EAL/HD-GYP).

Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks tightly clustered in glycine-rich loops and adjacent catalytic residues; dominant peaks at P-loop glycines and Lys/Thr, SGGQ of the C-loop, the Walker B DE pair, and nearby His/Gln; multiple discrete clusters per nucleotide-binding domain and duplicated blocks in proteins with two NBDs; additional peaks on histidine kinase HATPase_c N/G1/F/G2 boxes (Bergerat-fold glycine-rich loops and associated acidic residues), on phosphoacceptor Asp and Mg-binding acidic residues in receiver domains, on N-terminal GxGxxG loops adjacent to FAD/NAD-binding sites, and on EAL/HD-GYP catalytic Glu/Asp/His residues and coordinating metal-binding sites in c-di-GMP phosphodiesterases.

Exemplars:
- ABC importer ATPases (spermidine/putrescine, cobalt): activation on Walker A P-loop, LSGGQ signature, Walker B DE, and H-loop.
- ABC exporters (macrolide exporter MacB-like, peptide/secretion ABC ATPases): same NBD motif set within the cytosolic domain.
- Eukaryotic ABC transporters (ABCA/ABCB/ABCH): activation on NBD P-loop, C-loop, Walker B, with additional peaks at the Q-loop; duplicated clusters in full-length transporters with two NBDs.
- Ribosome-associated ABC ATPases (ABCF/ABCE-like): two mirrored activation blocks across both NBDs at P-loop, LSGGQ, and Walker B DE.
- Two-component systems: response regulator receiver domains (CheY-like) with peaks at the active-site phospho-Asp and Mg2+-binding acids; sensor histidine kinases with peaks at HATPase_c N/G1/F/G2 boxes.
- Flavin-dependent enzymes (flavin halogenases and related FAD binders): weaker activation on N-terminal glycine-rich Rossmann-like loops near the cofactor-binding site.
- c-di-GMP signaling enzymes (EAL/HD-GYP phosphodiesterases): activation on EAL or HD-GYP motifs and adjacent metal-coordinating residues.

neighbor_rows.label: Pre-motif redox positioning segment
neighbor_rows.summary: Short pre–active-site segment immediately N‑terminal to redox‑active cysteine/selenocysteine motifs in thiol‑based redox proteins; this includes Trx/PDI CXXC, deiodinase Sec, c‑type cytochrome CXXCH, glutaredoxin CGFS, peroxiredoxin TxxC, and Cys clusters that ligate redox cofactors (e.g., CxxxCxxC in radical‑SAM/NifB and the catalytic Cys pair in VKOR). The segment is the structured prelude that positions the motif; in thioredoxin‑like folds it is often a beta‑strand–loop–alpha‑helix junction, while in other folds (membrane/peripheral or radical‑SAM) it is the analogous short pre‑motif loop/turn. The motif residues themselves are not the primary target.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Short pre–active-site segment immediately N‑terminal to redox‑active cysteine/selenocysteine motifs in thiol‑based redox proteins; this includes Trx/PDI CXXC, deiodinase Sec, c‑type cytochrome CXXCH, glutaredoxin CGFS, peroxiredoxin TxxC, and Cys clusters that ligate redox cofactors (e.g., CxxxCxxC in radical‑SAM/NifB and the catalytic Cys pair in VKOR). The segment is the structured prelude that positions the motif; in thioredoxin‑like folds it is often a beta‑strand–loop–alpha‑helix junction, while in other folds (membrane/peripheral or radical‑SAM) it is the analogous short pre‑motif loop/turn. The motif residues themselves are not the primary target.
Activation pattern: Short 4–10 aa windows peaking ~−4 to −1 to the first motif Cys/Sec (or the first Cys of a Cys cluster); catalytic Cys/Sec have low/zero signal; typically one cluster per catalytic module/domain.
Exemplars: 
- Thioredoxin/thiol–disulfide oxidoreductases (Trx, DsbA/DsbC, PDI): pre‑CXXC segment.
- GILT: coil immediately N‑terminal to CXXC.
- Iodothyronine deiodinases: pre‑Sec strand/loop just before the helix with Sec.
- Glutaredoxins (di‑ and monothiol): pre‑CGFS segment of the Trx‑like active site.
- Peroxiredoxins: loop just N‑terminal to the peroxidatic Cys (TxxC) at the helix start.
- c‑type cytochromes: pre‑segment N‑terminal to the CXXCH heme‑attachment motif.
- VKORs and fused Trx‑like VKORs: pre‑motif segment before the catalytic Cys pair/partner CXXC.
- Radical‑SAM enzymes (e.g., NifB): pre‑segment immediately N‑terminal to the Fe–S‑ligating Cys cluster (CxxxCxxC).

neighbor_rows.label: Histidine-centered metal-binding motifs
neighbor_rows.summary: Histidine-centered divalent metal–coordination motifs—especially HxH/HxHxD histidyl clusters that chelate catalytic or structural metals (most often Zn2+, but also Fe2+, Ni2+, Mn2+/Mg2+)—in metalloenzymes and zinc-binding modules; the feature prioritizes the His ligands (and immediate neighbors) rather than acidic co‑ligands.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Histidine-centered divalent metal–coordination motifs—especially HxH/HxHxD histidyl clusters that chelate catalytic or structural metals (most often Zn2+, but also Fe2+, Ni2+, Mn2+/Mg2+)—in metalloenzymes and zinc-binding modules; the feature prioritizes the His ligands (and immediate neighbors) rather than acidic co‑ligands.
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks on one or more histidines, often as short H clusters/pairs (e.g., HxH, HxHxD); multiple separated His clusters can occur within a protein (multiple metal sites or repeated modules). Occasional weaker peaks appear on adjacent residues that flank or shape the motif (e.g., Gly, Asp/Glu, Gln). Minimal activation outside these localized sites.
Exemplars: - Amidohydrolase superfamily deaminases/deiminases (e.g., enamidase, pterin deaminase): strong peaks on the metal-ligating His residues in the active site; little/no signal on catalytic Glu/Asp.
- Metallo-β-lactamase–fold hydrolases/nucleases/phosphodiesterases (e.g., MBL-domain RNase, TATDN2 nuclease, cAMP/cGMP phosphodiesterase): peaks on the HxHxD/HxH histidines that coordinate catalytic metals; acidic co‑ligands show weaker or absent activation.
- C2H2-type zinc-finger transcription factors: peaks on the His pair within each finger that completes Zn2+ coordination.
- DNA ligases: concentrated peaks on an N‑terminal histidine-rich cluster preceding the ligase core, consistent with histidine-based metal-binding patches.
- Other enzymes with isolated histidines (e.g., D-galactarolactone isomerase): localized peaks at a nearby H (and sometimes an adjacent residue), matching the preference for histidine-centered metal-binding microenvironments.

neighbor_rows.label: GDSL/SGNH nucleophile elbow
neighbor_rows.summary: Catalytic nucleophile-elbow at a beta strand–turn–alpha helix junction centered on a G-D-S/GDSL motif, marking the catalytic Ser block of SGNH/GDSL serine hydrolases and acyl-modifying enzymes (notably extracellular O-acetylation systems); the same short, small/polar loop–helix template is weakly recognized in analogous donor/acceptor-binding loops of other transferases.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Catalytic nucleophile-elbow at a beta strand–turn–alpha helix junction centered on a G-D-S/GDSL motif, marking the catalytic Ser block of SGNH/GDSL serine hydrolases and acyl-modifying enzymes (notably extracellular O-acetylation systems); the same short, small/polar loop–helix template is weakly recognized in analogous donor/acceptor-binding loops of other transferases.
Activation pattern: Primarily regional activation over an 8–20 residue block spanning a beta strand–loop–alpha helix junction, with residue-level peaks on the Ser of the GDS/GDSL motif when present; often occurs near the N-terminus of the mature, secreted/periplasmic protein and can appear as multiple local patches (e.g., both the GDS block and a conserved H–W region in TBL O-acetyltransferases). The sequence core is enriched for G/D/S/T flanked by hydrophobic residues.
Exemplars: SGNH/GDSL serine hydrolases (e.g., acyloxyacyl hydrolase): peak at the catalytic Ser within the nucleophile elbow; Plant TBL/AXY O-acetyltransferases: activation on the GDS catalytic block and a second patch on the conserved H–W region; Bacterial alginate/capsule O-acetylation proteins: activation around the SGNH-like catalytic Ser block in periplasmic O-acetyltransferases/deacetylases; Sialic-acid O-acetylesterases/deacetylases: activation at the Ser-containing catalytic block; Carbohydrate sulfotransferases (CHST): weaker activation on PAPS-binding loop–helix segments; Phosphoethanolamine transferases (periplasmic catalytic domain, e.g., OpgE/EptA-like): activation on a beta–loop–helix segment adjacent to the active-site region; Acid phosphatases/phosphodiesterases: activation on an N-terminal beta–loop–helix segment lacking specific annotations, consistent with structural motif matching.

neighbor_rows.label: Proline-induced helix kinks
neighbor_rows.summary: Proline-centered helix‑kink/hinge sites, most commonly Pro residues embedded in transmembrane α‑helices of multi‑pass membrane proteins where they introduce local bends/flexibility for conformational switching; occasionally extends to analogous Pro at helix termini or helix–strand junctions in soluble proteins.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Proline-centered helix‑kink/hinge sites, most commonly Pro residues embedded in transmembrane α‑helices of multi‑pass membrane proteins where they introduce local bends/flexibility for conformational switching; occasionally extends to analogous Pro at helix termini or helix–strand junctions in soluble proteins.
Activation pattern: Residue‑level peaks almost exclusively on Proline, typically multiple per protein; concentrated within hydrophobic α‑helices (especially transmembrane segments) and at their boundaries; occasional weaker co‑peaks on nearby small/hydrophobic residues; in sensor kinases also present in HAMP and HisKA helical regions near catalytic/relay sites; sparse in long loops.
Exemplars: - GPCRs (opsins, peptide/amine and lipid receptors: melatonin, adenosine A2A, S1P, orphan GPCRs): activation on conserved Pro in TM2/4/5/6/7 that create helix kinks central to receptor activation.
- Two‑component histidine kinases: activation on Pro in the transmembrane segment, the HAMP helix, and an α‑helix of the HisKA domain a few residues from the phospho‑His, marking hinge points for signal transmission.
- ABC transporter permease subunits (MalG family): activation on Pro within multiple TM helices and at TM‑to‑TM kink regions.
- P‑type heavy‑metal ATPases (Cu/Zn/Cd transporters): activation on a Pro within a kinked TM helix and on Pro in cytosolic helices flanking TMs near metal‑binding Asp/Glu sites.
- Soluble oxidoreductases (thioredoxin): activation on Pro within a helix (including the Cys‑Gly‑Pro‑Cys motif) and at a coil linking a helix to a β‑strand, reflecting helix‑disrupting/turn‑forming Pro.

neighbor_rows.label: α/β-hydrolase nucleophile elbow motif
neighbor_rows.summary: Conserved α/β-hydrolase “nucleophile elbow” surrounding the catalytic nucleophile (most often Ser; also Asp/Cys) at the β-strand–loop–α-helix junction, typically a short Gly/His-enriched motif (e.g., G–X–S–X–G, G–H–S, H–D) that flanks the nucleophile and contributes to the oxyanion-hole environment.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Conserved α/β-hydrolase “nucleophile elbow” surrounding the catalytic nucleophile (most often Ser; also Asp/Cys) at the β-strand–loop–α-helix junction, typically a short Gly/His-enriched motif (e.g., G–X–S–X–G, G–H–S, H–D) that flanks the nucleophile and contributes to the oxyanion-hole environment.
Activation pattern: Residue-level peaks confined to a 5–10 aa window in the α/β-hydrolase core, maximal at the residue immediately N-terminal to the nucleophile (often a His) with signal extending to the nucleophile itself and its flanking Gly/small hydrophobics; localized to the β-strand preceding the nucleophile and into the start of the following helix. Minimal activation elsewhere in the protein; occasional weaker secondary peak near the catalytic acidic residue strand.
Exemplars: - Kynurenine formamidase (arylformamidase, α/β-hydrolase): peak at His just N-terminal to the catalytic Ser; weaker signal near a strand preceding the catalytic Asp.
- Lipid droplet hydrolase/lipase-like α/β-hydrolase: sharp focus on a GHSMG/GXSXG segment around the catalytic Ser at the strand–loop–helix transition; no signal on distal His/Asp of the triad.
- Epoxide hydrolase (α/β-hydrolase with Asp nucleophile): hotspot at His immediately before the catalytic Asp in the nucleophile elbow; other catalytic residues show little/no activation.
- Dipeptidyl peptidases (S9 family): activation on the conserved G–W–S segment containing the catalytic Ser within the α/β-hydrolase domain.
- Bacterial esterases/thioesterases (including siderophore- and biotin-pathway esterases) and plant hormone/pigment hydrolases: activation on the canonical GXSXG/G–H–S nucleophile motif at the β-strand–loop–helix junction.

neighbor_rows.label: Ser/Thr motif-proximal signal
neighbor_rows.summary: Ser/Thr-centric signal marking residues that sit in or immediately flank functional binding/regulatory motifs—most characteristically the conserved Thr/Ser of Rossmann-like NAD(P)-binding loops in SDR/oxidoreductases—and, more broadly, Ser/Thr positions adjacent to catalytic or metal-binding sites or within Ser/Thr-rich flexible regulatory segments.
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Ser/Thr-centric signal marking residues that sit in or immediately flank functional binding/regulatory motifs—most characteristically the conserved Thr/Ser of Rossmann-like NAD(P)-binding loops in SDR/oxidoreductases—and, more broadly, Ser/Thr positions adjacent to catalytic or metal-binding sites or within Ser/Thr-rich flexible regulatory segments.
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks on Ser and Thr (Val as a secondary tolerated residue), appearing as isolated positions or short Ser/Thr runs. In SDR/oxidoreductases, peaks are enriched near the N-terminus (≈5–25) at/next to the Rossmann NAD(P)-binding motif; in histidine kinases they cluster within loops of the cytosolic HATPase_c core (absent from transmembranes/HPt). Activations occur across secondary structures (β, α, loops), usually in well-structured regions (high pLDDT) but can also appear in disordered loops. Aromatic/acidic residues rarely activate.
Exemplars: - NAD(P)-dependent oxidoreductases (SDR family and related): strong peaks on Thr/Ser preceding/within the Rossmann NAD(P)-binding loop (e.g., TGxxxGIG or GxSxG) and on nearby NAD(P)-contacting elements; additional sites near the catalytic Tyr/Lys helix.
- 3-ketodihydrosphingosine reductase (TSC10-like): activation on Thr/Ser within/adjacent to annotated NADPH-binding motifs and residues contacting NADP(+).
- 2-(R)-hydroxypropyl-CoM dehydrogenase: discrete Thr peaks including an annotated NAD(+)-binding Thr and other Thr in structured elements.
- Two-component histidine kinases: scattered Thr/Ser peaks within the kinase (HATPase_c) domain loops/ATP-lid; no activation in transmembrane segments or most of the HPt domain.
- Sulfatases (arylsulfatase-like): Thr peaks in β-strands/α-helices adjacent to Ca2+-binding sites and near catalytic residues; the modified catalytic Ser itself is typically not highlighted.
- Ketoreductases with low-confidence regions: occasional activation falls in disordered loops (sometimes on non-Ser/Thr), consistent with tolerance for flexible Ser/Thr-rich segments.

neighbor_rows.label: SAM-MTase catalytic micro-motifs
neighbor_rows.summary: Short catalytic micro‑motifs in class I SAM‑dependent methyltransferases, typically the D/HPPY‑like His–aromatic–acidic loop (or an equivalent β→α junction immediately adjacent to the SAM‑binding pocket) that lines the active site across diverse methyltransferase families
neighbor_rows.description:
Summary: Short catalytic micro‑motifs in class I SAM‑dependent methyltransferases, typically the D/HPPY‑like His–aromatic–acidic loop (or an equivalent β→α junction immediately adjacent to the SAM‑binding pocket) that lines the active site across diverse methyltransferase families
Activation pattern: Residue‑level peaks in very short windows (2–10 aa), often one to a few residues, clustered in active‑site loops at β‑strand→α‑helix junctions near the Rossmann SAM‑binding site; enriched for His with adjacent Tyr/Phe/Trp and acidic residues (D/E), flanked by hydrophobics (V/L/I). In some families this collapses to a single hotspot glycine within the SAM‑loop immediately following a SAM‑binding residue.
Exemplars: - RNA cap guanine‑N7 methyltransferases (eukaryotic and viral capping modules): activation on the His/acidic–aromatic loop that stacks the cap guanine and abuts the catalytic elements of the SAM site.
- tRNA methyltransferases (TRM9‑family, METTL‑family): activation on the D/HPPY‑like catalytic loop that positions the target base for methyl transfer.
- Protein N‑terminal X‑Pro‑Lys methyltransferases (NTMT1/NTMT2): activation on the conserved DPPY/HPNY loop adjacent to the SAM pocket.
- Quinone/benzoquinone pathway O‑methyltransferases (e.g., UbiG/Coq/COMT‑like): activation on the HPPY/DPVW‑type catalytic loop lining the substrate pocket.
- BioC‑type malonyl‑ACP O‑methyltransferases (biotin synthesis, including fused BioCD/H): activation on the His–Tyr/acidic micro‑motif adjacent to SAM.
- Phospholipid/membrane‑lipid methylation enzymes: activation on short active‑site loops with His + aromatic + acidic residues near the SAM site.
- Cyclopropane mycolic‑acid synthase (MmaA2; SAM‑dependent): a single peak at the β→α junction glycine immediately following a SAM‑binding isoleucine, consistent with the same SAM‑proximal loop targeted in other families.

anchor_metadata.label: Serine hydrolase nucleophile elbow
anchor_metadata.summary: Catalytic nucleophile serine of serine hydrolases, specifically the conserved “nucleophile elbow” pentapeptide (e.g., GXSXG/GHSxG/GDSL) at a β→α junction in α/β‑hydrolase–like folds, across esterases/lipases/thioesterases and related serine proteases/transferases; the feature recognizes this structural/sequence motif even in inactive esterase‑like homologs.
anchor_metadata.description:
Summary: Catalytic nucleophile serine of serine hydrolases, specifically the conserved “nucleophile elbow” pentapeptide (e.g., GXSXG/GHSxG/GDSL) at a β→α junction in α/β‑hydrolase–like folds, across esterases/lipases/thioesterases and related serine proteases/transferases; the feature recognizes this structural/sequence motif even in inactive esterase‑like homologs.
Activation pattern: Predominantly residue-level peaks centered on a single serine in a short coil at the end of a β‑strand entering an α‑helix (β→α turn); occasional weak shoulders on immediately adjacent small residues or nearby loop positions; other catalytic‑triad residues (Asp/His) are typically not activated. Most proteins show 1–4 peaks, with multi‑modular assembly‑line enzymes showing one per TE/catalytic module.
Exemplars: - Siderophore esterases/trilactone hydrolases (IroE/IroD family): peak on the nucleophilic Ser at the β→α junction.
- BioH-like pimeloyl‑ACP methyl ester esterases: sharp peak on the annotated catalytic Ser; Asp/His of the triad remain silent.
- Mammalian BPHL/carboxylesterase-like hydrolases: dominant peak on the catalytic Ser with minor signal on an adjacent substrate‑binding residue.
- NRPS/PKS thioesterase domains: activation on the Ser within the GHSxG motif; multiple peaks in multi‑module systems.
- Cholinesterases and carboxylesterases: activation on the catalytic Ser in the GXSXG nucleophile elbow.
- Serine carboxypeptidases and dipeptidyl peptidases (α/β‑hydrolase catalytic domains): peak on the active‑site Ser.
- Mycobacterial Ag85 mycolyltransferases (SGNH/GDSL hydrolase‑like): activation on the catalytic Ser of the SGNH/GDSL motif.
- Inactive esterase‑like/pseudoenzymes: residual activation on the conserved nucleophile‑elbow serine despite loss of catalytic activity.
